title: Microsoft Q3 FY2025 Earnings Call Transcript

sections.prepared_remarks: Microsoft reporting Q3 revenue of $70.1 billion, up 10 percent year over year. Azure grew 34 percent, with AI contributing approximately 13 points to that growth. This marks the third consecutive quarter where AI contributed double-digit growth to Azure — a structural driver. Copilot for Microsoft 365 reached 850,000 paying organizations. Copilot Studio, our enterprise AI agent platform, has over 60,000 customers. GitHub Copilot Enterprise revenue grew 60 percent. We are launching Microsoft Copilot Agents — autonomous AI workers that handle business processes. Our security revenue hit $22 billion annualized. LinkedIn reached $4.5 billion quarterly revenue, up 9 percent. Surface revenue grew double digits driven by AI PCs. We are increasing fiscal 2026 investment in AI infrastructure, with capex guidance of $19 to $22 billion per quarter. Our AI datacenter expansion is ahead of schedule for the first time in several years. Copilot + Windows 11 AI features are driving PC upgrade cycles in enterprise — we estimate 70 percent of enterprise Windows devices will be refreshed with NPU-capable hardware over 24 months.
sections.financial_highlights: EPS $2.94, gross margin 71.5 percent. Operating income $27.5 billion, up 12 percent. Free cash flow $22 billion after $16.1 billion in capex. The gap between operating and free cash flow reflects our massive infrastructure investment cycle. We expect Q4 revenue of $72.5 to $73.5 billion, implying continued double-digit growth. Azure growth 33 to 35 percent in Q4, with 12-point AI contribution. Cloud gross margins are stabilizing as new GPU clusters reach steady state. Our data center utilization rates improved 15 percent quarter over quarter. The Office 365 Business subscription base grew 13 percent. We are seeing strong initial traction for Copilot Analytics — showing customers concrete productivity gains, which is the most effective sales driver we have.
sections.qanda_session:
Fred Havemeyer: Satya, on the Agentic Copilot product — can you help us think about the pricing and packaging versus consumption-based AI? Are agents sold as seats, or per workflow, or purely consumption-based? And roughly what percentage of your AI revenue today is per-seat versus consumption?

Satya Nadella: Fred, we price agents in two ways: consumption-based for automated workflows, and per-user subscription for embedded agent capabilities. Today consumption-based AI services represent about 60 percent of our AI revenue and per-seat about 40 percent. We expect agentic services to be majority consumption-based over time because agents run continuously and generate more compute. But the per-seat attach as a percentage of base subscriptions continues to rise — we're seeing IT buyers standardize on Copilot across entire departments, not just individual power users. The competitive dynamic is not really pricing — it's the fact that enterprise customers need AI that works with their proprietary data in their tenant. That requires Microsoft 365 integration, compliance, and security — things generic AI providers cannot deliver. That is the real moat.

John DiFucci: Amy, on the capital intensity — $16.1 billion in one quarter, and you just guided higher for fiscal 2026. Is there a point where cloud and AI infrastructure investment hits a saturation in terms of adding to earnings capacity? When does the capex cycle start to decelerate?

Amy Hood: John, that's the right question. We are investing well ahead of current revenue to capture the infrastructure lead. We expect capex to peak in fiscal Q2 2026 as the primary datacenter build-out reaches completion. Beginning in fiscal Q3 2026, we expect capex to normalize downward, likely to $10 to $12 billion per quarter. We model the return on investment over a 5-year horizon — the current infrastructure investments will generate cloud and AI revenue for a decade. Our operating leverage is improving: the incremental gross margin on incremental Azure revenue is approximately 65 percent, which is the highest in the industry. We expect operating income growth to acceleration in fiscal 2026 as utilization scales and new capacity is absorbed onto revenue-generating workloads.
sections.forward_outlook: Satya Nadella: The shift to AI-first software is happening faster than our internal models predicted three years ago. We are adding AI capabilities to every product — in the last 90 days we shipped over 150 AI features across the portfolio. The enterprise is adopting our AI stack because it integrates with things they already own: Microsoft 365, Dynamics, Power Platform, and Azure OpenAI. The combination of proprietary models, enterprise data in Microsoft Fabric, and Copilot across every surface is unique. We see a clear path to $500 billion in total addressable market for Microsoft by 2030. We have the balance sheet, the customer base, and the engineering depth to capture the majority of that opportunity. We are in the strongest competitive position in our company's history.
